item.title: When random is not actually random enough
item.description:
📝 Every object should have the same chance of being picked. That means that the variability of the chosen object you pick doesn’t respect what we might intuitively think: we might think every item has a 1/10 chance of being chosen. Assuming that our random choice function has a uniform distribution, every integer will have a chance of 1/10 = 10% of being chosen.
🔗 Read more: https://ersc.io/blog/when-random-isnt-random-enough

item.title: California closed the Montana license plate loophole
item.description:
📝 ” Essentially, if more than half of your business was held outside California, you could keep your vehicle registered to that out-of-state business without paying Use Tax in California. Say you live in Nevada and your vehicle is registered to your business based there; if you operate a branch office on the California side of Lake Tahoe, for instance, you could legally keep your car there on Nevada plates so long as the bulk of the business was based in Nevada. If anyone running the business is a California resident (by the updated definition outlined above), then the whole business is a California resident, and any assets (including Lamborghinis and Bugattis) held in the state are subject to California taxation.
🔗 Read more: https://www.thedrive.com/news/heres-how-california-closed-the-montana-license-plate-loophole
